scope: Version-specific source-context review of header/data record fixed fields CHROM, POS, ID, REF, ALT, QUAL, FILTER and INFO, plus conditional FORMAT/sample-column introduction, for VCFv4.1–4.5. This artifact does not exhaust genotype field grammar, reserved INFO/FORMAT tables, breakend syntax, symbolic allele definitions, or all cross-references.

lines.text: \subsection{Data lines}
\subsubsection{Fixed fields}
There are 8 fixed fields per record. All data lines are tab-delimited. In all cases, missing values are specified with a dot (`.'). Fixed fields are:
\begin{enumerate}

\item CHROM - chromosome: An identifier from the reference genome or an angle-bracketed ID String (``$<$ID$>$'') pointing to a contig in the assembly file (cf.\ the \#\#assembly line in the header). All entries for a specific CHROM should form a contiguous block within the VCF file. (String, no whitespace permitted, Required).

\item POS - position: The reference position, with the 1st base having position 1. Positions are sorted numerically, in increasing order, within each reference sequence CHROM.   It is permitted to have multiple records with the same POS. Telomeres are indicated by using positions 0 or N+1, where N is the length of the corresponding chromosome or contig.   (Integer, Required)

\item ID - identifier: Semicolon-separated list of unique identifiers where available. If this is a dbSNP variant it is encouraged to use the rs number(s). No identifier should be present in more than one data record. If there is no identifier available, then the missing value should be used. (String, no whitespace or semicolons permitted)

\item REF - reference base(s): Each base must be one of A,C,G,T,N (case insensitive). Multiple bases are permitted. The value in the POS field refers to the position of the first base in the String. For simple insertions and deletions in which either the REF or one of the ALT alleles would otherwise be null/empty, the REF and ALT Strings must include the base before the event (which must be reflected in the POS field), unless the event occurs at position 1 on the contig in which case it must include the base after the event; this padding base is not required (although it is permitted) for e.g.\ complex substitutions or other events where all alleles have at least one base represented in their Strings.  If any of the ALT alleles is a symbolic allele (an angle-bracketed ID String ``$<$ID$>$'') then the padding base is required and POS denotes the coordinate of the base preceding the polymorphism. Tools processing VCF files are not required to preserve case in the allele Strings. (String, Required).

\item ALT - alternate base(s): Comma separated list of alternate non-reference alleles.  These alleles do not have to be called in any of the samples.  Options are base Strings made up of the bases A,C,G,T,N, (case insensitive) or an angle-bracketed ID String (``$<$ID$>$'') or a breakend replacement string as described in the section on breakends. If there are no alternative alleles, then the missing value should be used.  Tools processing VCF files are not required to preserve case in the allele String, except for IDs, which are case sensitive.  (String; no whitespace, commas, or angle-brackets are permitted in the ID String itself)

\item QUAL - quality: Phred-scaled quality score for the assertion made in ALT. i.e.\ $-10log_{10}$ prob(call in ALT is wrong). If ALT is `.' (no variant) then this is $-10log_{10}$ prob(variant), and if ALT is not `.' this is $-10log_{10}$ prob(no variant). High QUAL scores indicate high confidence calls. Although traditionally people use integer phred scores, this field is permitted to be a floating point to enable higher resolution for low confidence calls if desired.  If unknown, the missing value should be specified. (Numeric)

\item FILTER - filter status: PASS if this position has passed all filters, i.e., a call is made at this position. Otherwise, if the site has not passed all filters, a semicolon-separated list of codes for filters that fail. e.g.\ ``q10;s50'' might indicate that at this site the quality is below 10 and the number of samples with data is below 50\% of the total number of samples. `0' is reserved and should not be used as a filter String. If filters have not been applied, then this field should be set to the missing value. (String, no whitespace or semicolons permitted)

\item INFO - additional information: (String, no whitespace, semicolons, or equals-signs permitted; commas are permitted only as delimiters for lists of values) INFO fields are encoded as a semicolon-separated series of short keys with optional values in the format: $<$key$>$=$<$data$>$[,data]. If no keys are present, the missing value must be used. Arbitrary keys are permitted, although the following sub-fields are reserved (albeit optional):
\begin{itemize}
\item AA : ancestral allele
\item AC : allele count in genotypes, for each ALT allele, in the same order as listed
\item AF : allele frequency for each ALT allele in the same order as listed: use this when estimated from primary data, not called genotypes
\item AN : total number of alleles in called genotypes
\item BQ : RMS base quality at this position
\item CIGAR : cigar string describing how to align an alternate allele to the reference allele
\item DB : dbSNP membership
\item DP : combined depth across samples, e.g.\ DP=154
\item END : end position of the variant described in this record (for use with symbolic alleles)
\item H2 : membership in hapmap2
\item H3 : membership in hapmap3
\item MQ : RMS mapping quality, e.g.\ MQ=52
\item MQ0 : Number of MAPQ == 0 reads covering this record
\item NS : Number of samples with data
\item SB : strand bias at this position
\item SOMATIC : indicates that the record is a somatic mutation, for cancer genomics
\item VALIDATED : validated by follow-up experiment
\item 1000G : membership in 1000 Genomes
\end{itemize}
\end{enumerate}
The exact format of each INFO sub-field should be specified in the meta-information (as described above).

Example for an INFO field: DP=154;MQ=52;H2. Keys without corresponding values are allowed in order to indicate group membership (e.g.\ H2 indicates the SNP is found in HapMap 2). It is not necessary to list all the properties that a site does NOT have, by e.g.\ H2=0. See below for additional reserved INFO sub-fields used to encode structural variants.
\subsubsection{Genotype fields}

If genotype information is present, then the same types of data must be present for all samples. First a FORMAT field is given specifying the data types and order (colon-separated alphanumeric String). This is followed by one field per sample, with the colon-separated data in this field corresponding to the types specified in the format. The first sub-field must always be the genotype (GT) if it is present.  There are no required sub-fields.

\label{data-lines}
All data lines are tab-delimited with no tab character at the end of the line.
The last data line must end with a line separator.

\begin{enumerate}

\item CHROM --- chromosome: An identifier from the reference genome or an angle-bracketed ID String (``$<$ID$>$'') pointing to a contig in the assembly file (cf.\ the \#\#assembly line in the header).

(String, no whitespace permitted, Required).
\item POS --- position: The reference position, with the 1st base having position 1.
Positions are sorted numerically, in increasing order, within each reference sequence CHROM.
It is permitted to have multiple records with the same POS.
Telomeres are indicated by using positions 0 or N+1, where N is the length of the corresponding chromosome or contig.
(Integer, Required)
\item ID --- identifier: Semicolon-separated list of unique identifiers where available.
If this is a dbSNP variant the rs number(s) should be used.
No identifier should be present in more than one data record.
If there is no identifier available, then the MISSING value should be used.
(String, no whitespace or semicolons permitted, duplicate values not allowed.)
\item REF --- reference base(s): Each base must be one of A,C,G,T,N (case insensitive).
Multiple bases are permitted.
The value in the POS field refers to the position of the first base in the String.

For simple insertions and deletions in which either the REF or one of the ALT alleles would otherwise be null/empty, the REF and ALT Strings must include the base before the event (which must be reflected in the POS field), unless the event occurs at position 1 on the contig in which case it must include the base after the event; \pagebreak[1] this padding base is not required (although it is permitted) for e.g.\ complex substitutions or other events where all alleles have at least one base represented in their Strings.
If any of the ALT alleles is a symbolic allele (an angle-bracketed ID String ``$<$ID$>$'') then the padding base is required and POS denotes the coordinate of the base preceding the polymorphism.
Tools processing VCF files are not required to preserve case in the allele Strings. (String, Required).

If the reference sequence contains IUPAC ambiguity codes not allowed by this specification (such as R = A/G), the ambiguous reference base must be reduced to a concrete base by using the one that is first alphabetically (thus R as a reference base is converted to A in VCF.)
\item ALT --- alternate base(s): Comma-separated list of alternate non-reference alleles.
These alleles do not have to be called in any of the samples.

Options are base Strings made up of the bases A,C,G,T,N (case insensitive) or the `*' symbol (allele missing due to overlapping deletion) or a MISSING value `.' (no variant) or an angle-bracketed ID String (``$<$ID$>$'') or a breakend replacement string as described in Section \ref{Breakends}.
If there are no alternative alleles, then the MISSING value must be used.
In other words, the ALT field must be a symbolic allele, or a breakend replacement string, or match the regular expression \texttt{\^{}([ACGTNacgtn]+|\string\*|\string\.)\$}.
Tools processing VCF files are not required to preserve case in the allele String, except for IDs, which are case sensitive.
(String; no whitespace, commas, or angle-brackets are permitted in the ID String itself)
\item QUAL --- quality: Phred-scaled quality score for the assertion made in ALT. i.e.\ $-10log_{10}$ prob(call in ALT is wrong).
If ALT is `.' (no variant) then this is $-10log_{10}$ prob(variant), and if ALT is not `.' this is $-10log_{10}$ prob(no variant).
If unknown, the MISSING value must be specified. (Float)
\item FILTER --- filter status: PASS if this position has passed all filters, i.e., a call is made at this position.

Otherwise, if the site has not passed all filters, a semicolon-separated list of codes for filters that fail. e.g.\ ``q10;s50'' might indicate that at this site the quality is below 10 and the number of samples with data is below 50\% of the total number of samples.
`0' is reserved and must not be used as a filter String.
If filters have not been applied, then this field must be set to the MISSING value.
(String, no whitespace or semicolons permitted, duplicate values not allowed.)
\item INFO --- additional information: Semicolon-separated series of additional information fields, or the MISSING value `{\tt .}'\ if none are present.
Each subfield consists of a short \emph{key} with optional \emph{values} in the format: key[=value[,\,\ldots,value]].

Literal semicolon (`{\tt ;}') and equals sign (`{\tt =}') characters are not permitted in these values, and literal commas (`{\tt ,}') are permitted only as delimiters for lists of values; characters with special meaning can be encoded using percent encoding, see Section~\ref{character-encoding}.
Space characters are allowed in values.
INFO keys must match the regular expression \texttt{\^{}([A-Za-z\_][0-9A-Za-z\_.]*|1000G)\$}, please note that ``1000G'' is allowed as a special legacy value.
Duplicate keys are not allowed.
Arbitrary keys are permitted, although those listed in Table~\ref{table:reserved-info} and described below are reserved (albeit optional).
The exact format of each INFO key should be specified in the meta-information (as described above).
Example of a complete INFO field: {\tt DP=154;MQ=52;H2}.
Keys without corresponding values may be used to indicate group membership (e.g.\ H2 indicates the SNP is found in HapMap 2).
See Section~\ref{sv-info-keys} for additional reserved INFO keys used to encode structural variants.

atomic_candidates.statement: Each VCF record has exactly eight fixed columns in the order CHROM, POS, ID, REF, ALT, QUAL, FILTER, INFO.
atomic_candidates.test_oracle: Parse record field count and positional names; reject fewer/more fixed columns while allowing sample columns only under genotype header contract.

atomic_candidates.statement: All records for a given CHROM form one contiguous block in the file.
atomic_candidates.test_oracle: A CHROM value that reappears after a different CHROM block is rejected.

atomic_candidates.statement: POS uses 1-based reference coordinates; position 1 is the first base.
atomic_candidates.test_oracle: Coordinate interpretation uses one-based positions; separate acceptance of telomeric 0 and N+1 is captured in REC-005.

atomic_candidates.statement: Within each reference sequence CHROM, POS values are numerically non-decreasing; equal POS values are explicitly permitted.
atomic_candidates.test_oracle: Reject a lower POS after a higher POS within a CHROM; allow equal POS. Do not impose a unique-position constraint.

atomic_candidates.statement: Telomeres may be represented with POS=0 or POS=N+1, where N is the contig length.
atomic_candidates.test_oracle: Accept the two specified telomere coordinates when contig length is known; do not reject solely for POS=0 or N+1.

atomic_candidates.statement: An identifier must not occur in more than one data record.
atomic_candidates.test_oracle: Reject reuse of the same non-missing identifier across distinct records; distinguish identifier list parsing and missing-value handling.

atomic_candidates.statement: ID is a semicolon-separated identifier list; identifiers cannot contain whitespace or semicolons.
atomic_candidates.test_oracle: Accept multiple identifiers separated by semicolon; reject whitespace or semicolon embedded within a token.

atomic_candidates.statement: If no identifier is available, ID uses the missing-value marker.
atomic_candidates.test_oracle: An absent identifier is represented by '.' rather than an empty field; do not treat this as a mandatory ID assertion.

atomic_candidates.statement: REF sequence characters are restricted to A,C,G,T,N, case-insensitively; multiple bases are permitted.
atomic_candidates.test_oracle: Accept one or more permitted bases regardless of case; reject disallowed symbols except where separately defined allele classes apply to ALT.

atomic_candidates.statement: POS identifies the reference coordinate of the first base in REF.
atomic_candidates.test_oracle: For a record with REF length >1, the first REF base maps to POS; do not mistake POS as an interbase coordinate.

atomic_candidates.topic: Indel padding away from first base
atomic_candidates.statement: For simple insertions/deletions with an otherwise empty REF or ALT allele, REF and ALT include the preceding base and POS reflects that padding base.
atomic_candidates.test_oracle: Validate preceding-base padding and POS for simple indels away from contig position 1.

atomic_candidates.statement: For a simple insertion/deletion at contig position 1, the following base is used as padding.
atomic_candidates.test_oracle: Validate following-base padding for simple indels at the first contig position.

atomic_candidates.statement: The padding base is not required, but is permitted, for complex substitutions or events where every allele has at least one represented base.
atomic_candidates.test_oracle: Accept both padded and unpadded representations in the explicitly exempt complex-allele case.

atomic_candidates.statement: If any ALT allele is symbolic, the required padding base is present and POS denotes the coordinate of the preceding base.
atomic_candidates.test_oracle: Reject symbolic ALT records lacking required padding, except version-defined explicit exceptions such as <*>.

atomic_candidates.statement: A VCF processing tool is not required to preserve allele-string case.
atomic_candidates.test_oracle: A reader must not reject solely because a producer normalizes allele-string case; a writer may canonicalize case.

atomic_candidates.statement: ALT is a comma-separated list of non-reference alleles and may include allele forms defined by the applicable version (sequence, spanning-deletion *, missing '.', symbolic allele, breakend; VCFv4.4+ also unspecified allele <*>).
atomic_candidates.test_oracle: Validate each comma-delimited ALT allele against version-scoped alternatives; preserve symbolic and breakend grammars as delegated sub-specifications.

atomic_candidates.topic: ALT need not be observed in samples
atomic_candidates.statement: ALT alleles listed in a record do not have to be called in any sample.
atomic_candidates.test_oracle: Do not require every ALT allele to occur in sample GT calls.

atomic_candidates.statement: If no alternative alleles are present, ALT is represented by the missing-value marker.
atomic_candidates.test_oracle: Accept ALT='.' for no alternative alleles; do not accept an empty ALT field.

atomic_candidates.statement: QUAL is a Phred-scaled quality for the ALT assertion; its probability interpretation reverses when ALT='.' versus ALT not '.'.
atomic_candidates.test_oracle: Interpret score against P(variant) when ALT='.' and P(no variant) when ALT is non-missing; unknown score uses '.'.

atomic_candidates.statement: FILTER is PASS if all filters pass; otherwise it lists failing filter codes separated by semicolons.
atomic_candidates.test_oracle: Parse PASS distinctly from filter IDs and missing value; split multiple failure codes on semicolon.

atomic_candidates.statement: The filter identifier '0' is reserved and must not be used as a FILTER string in VCFv4.3–4.5; earlier versions say it should not be used.
atomic_candidates.test_oracle: Reject FILTER identifier 0 under 4.3–4.5; report a SHOULD-level violation under 4.1–4.2.

atomic_candidates.statement: If filters have not been applied, FILTER is the missing-value marker.
atomic_candidates.test_oracle: Do not encode not-evaluated filters as PASS; use '.'.

atomic_candidates.statement: INFO is a semicolon-separated list of key or key=value entries; '.' represents no INFO entries.
atomic_candidates.test_oracle: Parse semicolon-delimited entries with optional values and use '.' for no entries; empty INFO is invalid.

atomic_candidates.statement: Literal semicolons and equals signs are prohibited within INFO values; commas are permitted only as list delimiters; VCFv4.3+ permits special characters via percent encoding.
atomic_candidates.test_oracle: Reject raw reserved delimiters in values; interpret percent-encoded special characters per character-encoding section where applicable.

atomic_candidates.statement: VCFv4.3–4.5 INFO keys match the versioned regular expression; 1000G is an explicit legacy exception.
atomic_candidates.test_oracle: Validate INFO key against the regex and special-case 1000G; do not infer this exact grammar for 4.1–4.2.

atomic_candidates.statement: Duplicate INFO keys are not allowed in VCFv4.3–4.5.
atomic_candidates.test_oracle: Reject a record with repeated INFO key; preserve separate same-key values only where an explicitly defined syntax permits them.

atomic_candidates.statement: The exact format of each INFO key should be specified in header meta-information.
atomic_candidates.test_oracle: Validate declaration linkage using exact force and scope; reserved optional keys do not imply every listed key must appear.

atomic_candidates.statement: Genotype columns are present only when genotype information is present; FORMAT precedes the sample columns.
atomic_candidates.test_oracle: Distinguish sites-only records from genotype-bearing records and validate FORMAT/sample column layout only when genotype columns are present.

version_delta_observations.delta: VCFv4.1–4.2 describe eight fixed fields in the data-lines subsection; VCFv4.3–4.5 separately label header-line mandatory columns and data-line fixed fields.

VCFv4.1 allows sequence bases and symbolic/breakend forms; VCFv4.2 adds '*' spanning-deletion allele; VCFv4.3 provides explicit regex and MISSING semantics; VCFv4.4–4.5 explicitly add '<*>' unspecified allele.
VCFv4.1–4.2 label QUAL Numeric; VCFv4.3–4.5 label it Float.
VCFv4.1–4.2 say 0 should not be used; VCFv4.3–4.5 strengthen this to must not.
The explicit key regex and duplicate-key prohibition are present in VCFv4.3–4.5; do not back-propagate without source evidence.
VCFv4.3–4.5 add a rule for reducing disallowed IUPAC ambiguity in the reference sequence to the alphabetically first concrete base.
VCFv4.4–4.5 include '<*>' and the exception to ordinary symbolic-allele padding; it is not present in the VCFv4.1–4.3 ALT enumeration.

review.atomicity_review: PRIMARY_REVIEWED; SPLIT AND FORCE AUDIT REQUIRED

limitations: All excerpts are pinned to HTS specs commit 510c107ba89aa13113818c9e4fa3071283cb7f7b; VCFv4.0 is excluded pending historical source byte capture.
Normative force labels for descriptive field definitions and cross-references require a separate clause-level interpretation review; candidate wording is not a legalistic force determination.

The source says CHROM blocks are contiguous and POS is sorted within each CHROM; a production validator must define and test the precise relationship between these two order constraints without inventing stronger sort keys.
REF reference-sequence normalization and handling of IUPAC ambiguity are distinct producer/reader responsibilities and need explicit actor assignment.
The record grammar's delegated breakend, symbolic allele, and percent-encoding sub-specifications are not expanded in this artifact.
